goalpost_prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: original render-locked catalogue goalpost for a LEGO-compatible City Prompt building family
Primary request: Create a high-end photorealistic architectural survey image of an ORIGINAL contemporary Calgary missing-middle townhome row inspired by the documented material and massing vocabulary of RNDSQR projects, without copying any single real building.
Scene/backdrop: quiet established inner-city Calgary residential street on a clear neutral late-summer afternoon; restrained mature street trees only at the outer frame; simple sidewalk, narrow landscaped front setbacks, no adjacent building blocking the subject.
Subject: one complete row of exactly FOUR attached ground-oriented townhomes, canonical overall dimensions approximately 28 metres wide by 14 metres deep, exactly THREE occupied storeys. Each 7-metre home must read as a distinct vertical bay sharing party walls. Alternate each bay by a shallow 0.45-metre front setback and by switching dominant charcoal-black fine corrugated/flat metal cladding with warm natural cedar identity panels. Every home has its own deeply recessed street door, short concrete stoop, slim black canopy, address-light box without readable text, and a narrow planted strip. Use large but residential-scale black-framed picture windows, separate operable lites, recessed dark low-e glazing, occasional cedar privacy fins, and one restrained second-floor Juliet guard per alternating unit. Keep a coherent structural window cadence rather than random openings. The third floor steps back slightly behind a slim parapet; each home has a private rooftop terrace with black open railings and a compact charcoal stair bulkhead. The row ends have believable side returns, downpipes, flashing and window hierarchy. No garage doors on the street facade; rear-lane garages remain hidden behind the row.
Style/medium: premium photoreal architectural photography, physically plausible construction, fine material scale, subtle real weathering, not illustration or concept art.
Composition/framing: full building visible edge to edge from a front-left street-corner camera at pedestrian eye level, approximately 28–35 mm architectural lens, verticals straight, both the complete front elevation and left return visible, generous margin around roofline and ground.
Lighting/mood: broad neutral daylight with soft directional definition and readable contact shadows; no sunset orange, no cinematic glow.
Materials/textures: matte charcoal corrugated metal with correctly scaled ribs, flat black metal cassette accents, honey-toned vertical cedar boards with individual grain and narrow joints, pale warm-grey concrete stoops, black powder-coated steel, dark neutral low-e glass with restrained reflections and sparse warm occupied depth behind it.
Constraints: exactly four attached homes and exactly three occupied storeys; preserve the complete row in frame; individual front doors must remain visible; rooftop terraces must be physically plausible; all cladding changes align to unit boundaries and construction joints; original design only; no logos, no readable signs, no watermark.
Avoid: generic apartment block, monolithic box, detached houses, five or more units, extra floors, suburban garages facing the street, red brick, white stucco dominance, blue mirror glass, random checkerboard windows, fake balconies, impossible cantilevers, decorative mountain roof peaks, people crowding the facade, cars blocking the building, dramatic sunset, painterly rendering, text.

Input images: Image 1 is the approved ORIGINAL townhome goalpost and is the hard authority for identity, four-unit count, three-storey height, material schedule, window cadence, entrances and rooftop terraces.
Primary request: Create a precise straight-on orthographic FRONT ELEVATION of the exact same four-home Cedar & Black-Metal missing-middle row shown in Image 1.
Scene/backdrop: isolated complete facade on a plain warm light-grey studio field with one thin neutral ground datum; no street scene, adjacent houses, vegetation, furniture, vehicles or people.
Subject: preserve exactly FOUR attached 7-metre townhouse bays and exactly THREE occupied levels. Keep each unit boundary, alternating charcoal fine-corrugated metal and honey cedar identity fields, four individual deeply recessed doors and concrete stoops, slim black canopies, the same large black-framed picture-window groups and narrow operable lites, cedar privacy-fin accents, low ground windows, parapet steps, four rooftop terrace railings and four compact stair bulkheads. Show party-wall separation through shallow facade offsets and vertical construction joints. Preserve the quiet residential scale and do not combine windows into apartment ribbons.
Style/medium: high-fidelity photoreal architectural survey elevation, physically plausible materials, fine cladding scale, no illustration.
Composition/framing: camera perfectly perpendicular to the public facade, zero perspective convergence, all four units centered and visible edge-to-edge, both end edges visible, complete roof equipment and ground line included, generous even margin.
Lighting/mood: broad diffuse overcast studio light, shadow-neutral enough for albedo registration; only restrained contact occlusion in recesses.
Materials/textures: correctly scaled matte charcoal corrugated ribs, flat-black flashings, narrow vertical cedar boards with natural grain, warm-grey concrete, black powder-coated frames and guards, dark neutral low-e glass with sparse low-contrast occupied depth.
Constraints: preserve Image 1's architecture without redesign; exactly four homes and three occupied levels; no moved or invented openings, no extra terraces, no pitched roofs, no garage doors, no readable text, no logos, no watermark.
Avoid: perspective, side view, generic monolithic apartment block, random window pattern, white stucco, brick, blue mirror glass, orange interior glow, dramatic sunlight, baked trees or cast shadows.
aerial_prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: render-locked aerial and roof-topology reference for a LEGO-compatible 3D building family
Input images: Image 1 is the approved street-corner goalpost; Image 2 is the approved rectified elevation. Both describe the exact same original four-home Cedar & Black-Metal townhome row and are hard invariants.
Primary request: Show that exact building from a high front-left three-quarter aerial angle so its complete 28-by-14-metre massing, four dwelling divisions, roof terraces and rear service edge can be constructed accurately.

Subject: preserve exactly FOUR attached townhomes and exactly THREE occupied levels. Each unit has its own usable flat rooftop terrace with open black steel railings and one compact charcoal stair-access bulkhead set toward the rear half. Show subtle membrane roof falls, scuppers/downpipes, slim copings and flashings. At the rear, provide one lane-loaded single garage door per unit integrated into the ground level, with simpler dark metal cladding, residential rear windows and a very shallow private terrace or landing above only where structurally plausible. Party-wall/parapet separations align exactly with the four 7-metre bays. End walls have quieter but complete window and drainage logic.
Style/medium: premium photoreal architectural survey render, physically plausible construction and fine material scale, not concept art.
Composition/framing: full building and every roof terrace visible, high front-left oblique, public elevation still recognizable, no crop, straight verticals.
Lighting/mood: neutral broad daylight with restrained contact shadows and no dramatic color cast.
Materials/textures: matte charcoal fine corrugated metal, flat black copings, honey cedar boards, dark low-e glazing, black railings, pale concrete stoops, dark membrane roofs.
Constraints: do not change the approved front architecture; exactly four homes and three occupied storeys; four distinct rooftop terraces; flat roofs only; rear garages face the lane, never the public street; no extra wings, towers, bridges, pitched roofs, text, logos or watermark.
Avoid: generic apartment slab, one continuous undivided roof deck, ornamental roof peaks, suburban front garages, huge mechanical equipment, blue curtain wall, red brick, landscaping that hides construction, dramatic sunset.
rear_elevation_prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural
Asset type: rectified render-locked rear service elevation for a LEGO-compatible 3D building family
Input images: Image 1 is the approved public street goalpost; Image 2 is the approved aerial/roof reference. They show the same original four-home Cedar & Black-Metal townhome row and are hard invariants for unit count, material identity, height and roof topology.
Primary request: Create a precise straight-on orthographic REAR ELEVATION of that exact building, showing a believable Calgary lane-loaded service edge without altering the approved public façade or roofline.

Subject: exactly FOUR attached 7-metre townhouse bays and exactly THREE occupied levels. Ground level has one restrained dark single-car lane garage door per dwelling, set within charcoal metal cladding, plus one narrow glazed pedestrian door per unit. Upper floors use a quieter repeat of the public materials: dark recessed low-e windows aligned to rooms, limited honey cedar identity panels, charcoal fine-corrugated fields, slim black Juliet guards on alternating bays, and precisely located downpipes. Preserve the four separate flat rooftop terraces, open black railings and four compact charcoal stair bulkheads visible above the parapet. Party-wall joints and slight façade offsets align with all four bays. No balconies projecting over the lane; only shallow inset upper-level openings.
Style/medium: high-fidelity photoreal architectural survey elevation, physically plausible construction, fine cladding scale, no illustration.
Composition/framing: camera perfectly perpendicular to the rear façade, zero perspective convergence, complete width, both ends, full roof equipment and ground line visible with generous even margin.
Lighting/mood: broad diffuse overcast studio light, shadow-neutral enough for material registration, restrained recess occlusion only.
Materials/textures: matte charcoal fine-corrugated steel, flat-black flashings, honey cedar vertical boards, dark neutral low-e glass, black powder-coated guards, dark insulated garage doors, pale concrete lane apron.
Constraints: exactly four homes, exactly three occupied levels, exactly four garage doors, exactly four rooftop terraces and four stair bulkheads; preserve the input design identity; no front-facing garages; no extra wings, floors, balconies, pitched roofs, logos, readable text or watermark.
Avoid: generic apartment back, giant industrial loading doors, white vinyl, red brick, blue mirror glass, random openings, projecting decks, trash clutter, cars, dramatic sunlight, orange glow, perspective or side view.
occupied_depth_prompt:
Use case: texture/skin source
Asset type: shadow-neutral occupied-depth plate for layered architectural glazing in a physically based 3D model
Primary request: Create a perfectly straight-on square atlas of subtle contemporary townhouse interior depth, intended to sit several centimetres behind dark low-e glass in the approved Cedar & Black-Metal four-home family.
Scene/backdrop: fill the frame with a clean 4-by-4 grid of sixteen varied residential room glimpses, each cell bounded by a thin nearly-black mullion; no exterior façade, no reflected sky, no people, text or view through to outdoors.
Subject: quiet believable Calgary townhouse interiors at normal residential scale: pale warm plaster walls, oak cabinetry and shelving, linen curtains, restrained plants, occasional pendant or floor lamp, shadowed circulation, a few dining or living silhouettes, and mostly unlit rooms. Vary the layouts enough to prevent repetition while keeping a coherent understated contemporary palette. Details should be low contrast and slightly softened because they will be viewed behind glazing.
Style/medium: premium photoreal architectural interior photography compressed into a reusable depth atlas; physically plausible, not an illustration.
Composition/framing: camera perpendicular to every room cell; no perspective convergence across the atlas; each cell is a complete modular rectangular room view with uncluttered edges suitable for cropping and tiling.
Lighting/mood: neutral daylight dominates; only sparse low-intensity warm practical lamps in about one quarter of cells; deep but readable interior shadows; no orange glow wash.
Materials/textures: warm off-white plaster, light oak, charcoal metal details, neutral textiles, restrained green planting.
Constraints: exactly 4 by 4 modular cells; thin dark separators; subtle low-contrast occupied depth; no exterior window glass baked over the rooms; no logos, readable text, faces or watermark.
Avoid: luxury showroom, hotel lobby, office interiors, people, bright televisions, saturated art, repeated identical rooms, strong perspective, blown-out lamps, blue reflections, dramatic cinematic lighting, exterior building façade.

material_prompts.cedar:

Asset type: shadow-neutral photoreal material source for a physically based 3D architectural skin
Primary request: Create a perfectly front-facing, seamless, square material study of premium natural western red cedar vertical rainscreen boards for the approved Cedar & Black-Metal missing-middle townhome family.
Scene/backdrop: the entire frame is the cladding surface; no building, corners, openings, hardware, landscape, text or border.
Subject: narrow vertical cedar boards approximately 90 millimetres face width with precise 8 millimetre dark recessed joints; varied but restrained honey, amber and light brown boards; authentic individual straight grain, a few subtle knots, slight board-to-board tone variation, clean contemporary exterior finish. The texture must read at true architectural scale and tile seamlessly left-to-right and top-to-bottom.
Style/medium: high-resolution photoreal orthographic albedo capture suitable as a source for color, roughness, normal and displacement maps; physically plausible, construction-document clarity.
Composition/framing: camera exactly perpendicular to the cladding, no perspective, no vignette, uniform scale across the frame.
Lighting/mood: broad diffuse neutral-white studio illumination, completely shadow-neutral and color-calibrated; no directional highlights, cast shadows, sunlight or ambient occlusion baked into the image.
Materials/textures: dry matte cedar with fine grain and subtle pores; narrow deep charcoal joints; no glossy varnish.
Constraints: seamless tile; full-frame material only; vertical grain and boards; consistent joint spacing; neutral white balance; no logos, readable markings or watermark.
Avoid: horizontal siding, diagonal boards, fake plastic wood, exaggerated knots, orange saturation, grey weathered barnwood, dramatic light, reflections, perspective, macro blur, screws, plants, windows, doors, architectural scene.
